nodes.name: Daily Schedule
nodes.notes: Starts the workflow on a timer — daily at 6:00. No input data; downstream nodes fetch what they need.

nodes.name: Read Source Feed
nodes.notes: Pulls the RSS feed and emits one item per entry (title, link, content). Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: Skip Already-Seen Posts
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Keep Top Stories
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 5 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
nodes.notes: Single fixed LLM step (no tool choice) — cheaper and more predictable than an agent. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run.

nodes.name: OpenAI Chat Model
nodes.notes: Chat model powering the AI step (model: gpt-4o-mini). Swap providers here without rewiring. Credential: OpenAI API key. platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.

nodes.name: Publish to Microsoft Teams
nodes.notes: Posts a chat message into a Microsoft Teams channel — same role as a Slack notify, for teams standardized on Teams. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Microsoft OAuth2. Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.

nodes.name: Publish to Slack
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack (#reporting) — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Confirm Cross-Post
nodes.notes: Rejoins 2 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Log Published Posts (Airtable)
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Metrics' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Align Field Names
nodes.notes: Normalizes field names so every source feeds the same downstream schema.

nodes.name: Cap Batch Volume
nodes.notes: Caps the stream at 25 items to protect downstream quotas.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

# Compile a daily digest: Slack & Airtable

**Pattern:** Scheduled Digest · **Level:** Intermediate · **Trigger:** Scheduled

## Overview

Runs on a schedule, and covers dashboards work end to end across Slack, Airtable and Microsoft Teams.

It moves through 15 working steps plus a 2-node error rail, in this order:

1. Daily Schedule
2. Read Source Feed
3. Skip Already-Seen Posts
4. Keep Top Stories
5. Rewrite for Our Audience (AI)
6. OpenAI Chat Model
7. Publish to Microsoft Teams
8. Publish to Slack
9. Confirm Cross-Post
10. Log Published Posts (Airtable)
11. Align Field Names
12. Cap Batch Volume
13. Summarize Run Stats
14. Append Audit Row (Airtable)
15. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing dashboards work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

Daily Schedule → Read Source Feed → Skip Already-Seen Posts → Keep Top Stories → Rewrite for Our Audience (AI) → OpenAI Chat Model → Publish to Microsoft Teams → Publish to Slack → Confirm Cross-Post → Log Published Posts (Airtable) → Align Field Names → Cap Batch Volume → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Airtable) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Airtable aligned by hand for dashboards
- Dashboards work where "Read Source Feed" is still a manual step before Slack
- Dashboards work that only reaches Slack on a schedule, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Airtable in step for dashboards, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Airtable are skipped, across all 17 nodes of this dashboards build
- A failed Slack or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 17 nodes in this dashboards build
- The dashboards AI step is isolated from Slack, so models swap without touching the other 17 nodes
- Fans the same result out to Microsoft Teams in the same run, for dashboards

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Microsoft OAuth2; OpenAI API key; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Deduplication is cross-execution, not just within a single run — an RSS feed re-serves the same items on every poll, and without this the same story would get posted again on every scheduled check.

## Practice exercises

You've got the basics covered — push further:

1. Turn off the AI rewrite step and compare the raw feed text against the rewritten version.
2. Add a second RSS source and merge both into one feed before dedupe.
3. Change 'Keep Top Stories' from 5 to 1 and see how it changes posting cadence.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**OpenAI API key**
platform.openai.com → API keys → create new secret key.
_Gotcha:_ Needs billing set up; a brand-new key with no credit returns 429 immediately.

**Microsoft OAuth2**
Azure Portal → App registrations → new app → add Microsoft Graph delegated permissions.
_Gotcha:_ Graph throttles with HTTP 429 — the retry setting on this node already handles it.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**AI node fails with an auth or quota error**
Cause: API key missing billing, or the per-minute rate limit was hit.
Fix: Confirm the provider account has credit. For rate limits, lower concurrency or switch to a higher-quota model.

**The AI returns the wrong shape or rambles**
Cause: The prompt is under-specified for the task.
Fix: Tighten the System Message: state the role, the constraints, and the exact output format you expect.

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🤖 AI cluster

Purple nodes form one AI unit: the root node orchestrates, sub-nodes plug in via typed ports (model / memory / tools / parser). Swap the chat model without rewiring anything else. Costs scale with tokens — keep prompts lean and cap iterations.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your dashboards process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Microsoft Teams: restrict the app registration to the target team; tenant-wide permission is not needed to post.

**Do not log**
Log the identifier and the outcome, not the whole dashboards payload. n8n stores execution data verbatim, so anything a node emits is readable by everyone with instance access.
